title: Tiered Admission Shield and Eviction Contract for Rate Stability
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: During multi-tenant bursts and regional outages we observe unfair token draining, long tail latency spikes, and brittle limiter failovers. Current emergency responses (global hard-shed or region-level circuit breakers) cause either disproportionate customer outages or loss of SLO guarantees for critical tiers. Goal: introduce a Tiered Admission Shield (TAS) that provides graceful degradation with tenant-priority preservation and a formalized "eviction contract" to allow temporary scoped preemption and deterministic recovery.
acceptance_criteria: TAS implements admission tiers (critical, standard, best-effort) with configurable capacities per region and cross-region fallback order
Eviction contract enables short-lived preemption tokens that can be granted/revoked with lease semantics (TTL + renewal) and persisted to the global coordinator for rejoin reconciliation
Fairness goals verified: no tenant in a higher tier loses more than 10% of baseline throughput during a simulated 5x burst from other tenants
End-to-end integration tests exist that exercise limiter outage->recovery path and validate no token double-allocation after coordinator failover
Runbook pages and console alerts created; SLO impact projection for a 1-hour outage is documented
design_decisions: Introduce a lightweight local admission buffer per node that accepts requests up to a node-local soft limit before consulting the global coordinator — reduces coordinator pressure during microbursts
Eviction contract modeled as a lease object (tenant_id, tier, tokens_reserved, expires_at, preemption_reason) replicated via the existing region-broker (no new global DB dependency)
Priority preservation: admission always respects tier ordering; within tier, probabilistic weighted fairness based on recent token consumption windows
Circuit-breaker interaction: node-level circuit breaker trips to 'defer' (enqueue to local buffer) before 'reject', allowing short spikes to be absorbed without immediate 503s
Backpressure policy: when buffer fills, best-effort tier requests receive a fast path reject with a structured Retry-After and explanation code to surface to SDKs
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated rollout per region (ff:tas_local_buffer and ff:tas_eviction_contract)
Canary 2% of traffic in a non-prod-like region for 48h with synthetic burst tests
Increase to 25% after 72h if error/latency budgets remain healthy; monitor fairness metrics
Full roll to region after 7 days with degradation-mode telemetry validated
Cross-region enablement after all regions have coordinator minor-version; coordinate with infra on migration window
testing_plan: Unit tests for lease lifecycle (grant, renew, revoke, expiry)
Integration tests: simulate node crash during eviction contract active and validate deterministic recovery and token reallocation
Load tests: 10k qps mixed-tenant burst scenarios with 1,000 tenants to validate fairness bounds
Chaos tests: zone failure + delayed replication to ensure no split-brain token allocation
Regression tests to ensure SDK error codes/Retry-After semantics unchanged for client tooling
telemetry_and_alerts: New metrics: tas.local_buffer_fill_ratio, tas.lease_grants_per_minute, tas.eviction_revocations, tas.tenant_unfairness_index
SLO dashboards: latency p95/p99 by tier and tenant, and relative throughput loss vs baseline
Alert: tas.eviction_revocations > 5/min for 3m -> Investigate cross-tenant pressure or misconfiguration
Runbook alert: coordinator lag > 2s and local_buffer_fill_ratio > 0.8 -> shift region to degraded routing policy
Create a cost telemetry view showing extra tokens consumed during TAS absorption to forecast billing/credits
rollback_conditions: Unbounded growth in tas.local_buffer leading to > 10% headroom loss on nodes
Observed unfairness index > 0.25 for more than 15 minutes (indicating a fairness regression)
Coordinator version incompatibility causing lease reconciler exceptions > 0.1% of limiter calls
Unexpected increase in 5xx errors attributable to TAS path per tracing correlation
